Written by the rung worker for the gather's fold. Commits on `wip/rung-closure-name-once`: `17f3e7b17b` (the fix and its tests), `39f833b8e5` (the compiled test's generic trait case), and the commit that adds this record and `REPORT.md`. Lines cited are the branch's.

## Findings

1. **Each function expression of a component, and each local function, now has a class of its own: the first at a source span takes the name `<component>$fn@<span>`, as before, and each later one at that span the name with `#2`, `#3`, in the order in which the code generator meets them.** Conditions: the compiled path, both libraries; a generic closure's class file is `...#k⟦⟧`. Evidence: `NamingCzar.gensymArrowClassName` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/NamingCzar.java:893-907`) with the component's set `closureClassNames` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:386`, `:409`, `:4241-4244`), passed by `forFnExpr` (`:3935-3936`) and `localFunctionClosure` (`:4098-4099`). On the base's code `compiler_tests/ConditionalReductionCompiled.test` dies 'java.util.zip.ZipException: duplicate entry: ConditionalReductionCompiled$\=fn@7\!36-50.class' ('Tests run: 2,  Failures: 2', `old-fortress.sh ... junit .../ConditionalReductionCompiled.test`) and `one_library_tests/OneLibraryConditionalReduction.test` 'duplicate entry: OneLibraryConditionalReduction$\=fn@6\!56-79.class' ('Tests run: 2,  Failures: 1', under `FORTRESS_LIBRARY=one`); after, the first prints `PASS`, in a function, a generic at two instances and a generic trait's method, and the second compiles (`ant testFast`, compiler 'Tests run: 1738, Failures: 0', onelibrary 'Tests run: 5, Failures: 0'). What it means: row 315 closes; no class name of a program that compiled before changes.
2. **The two function expressions that share a span are the thunk that a conditional operator makes of its right operand and the outer closure of the reduction that is that operand.** Conditions: `x OP: (reduction)`, the operand a reduction alone, in parentheses or not; the same holds for any thunk of an operand that is a reduction. Evidence: the pre-disambiguation desugaring's `cleanupOpExpr` wraps the operand in `thunk`, a `fn () => e` at `e`'s span (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/desugarer/PreDisambiguationDesugaringVisitor.java:301-304`, `:333`), after `visitAccumulator` has rewritten the reduction at its span (`:454-494`) into `__bigOperator(op, fn (reduction, unit) => __generate(...))`, whose closure `DesugarerUtil.visitGenerators` makes at the same span (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/DesugarerUtil.java:194-197`); the loop body takes the generator clause's span (`:127`). The base's trace (`bin/fortress compile -debug codegen`, under the selector): 'forFnExpr className = AndRange$fn@3:56-79 desc = AbstractArrow??,...FBoolean?' then 'forFnExpr className = AndRange$fn@3:56-79 desc = AbstractArrow?Tuple?fortress/FortressLibrary$Reduction?...'. After the edit, `javap -p`: `fn@7:36-50` has `apply()`, `fn@7:36-50#2` has `apply(fortress.CompilerLibrary$ReductionZZ32, ...)`. What it means: the thunk, which the code generator meets first, keeps the span's name.
3. **The prelude can write the form: a program's own conditional operator over a `SUM` meets row 315 under the compiler's prelude.** Conditions: an operator declared at a thunk, as `opr ADDLAZY(a: ZZ32, b: () -> ZZ32): ZZ32`, and `n ADDLAZY: (SUM[i <- 0#n] i)`; any binary operator is conditional with a colon (`Specification/basic/operators/conditionalops.tex:14-20`; `Specification/advanced/subscripting.tex:90-91`). Evidence: finding 1's failing run of `ConditionalReductionCompiled` on the base. What it means: row 315's note "the prelude cannot write the form (no `zip`, no `BIG AND`)" was wrong; its repair has a test that runs.
4. **The names do not depend on a hash order or on what the JVM compiled before.** Conditions: the set is made with the component's `CodeGen` and only added to; two function expressions at one span lie one inside the other in one body, so the order is the tree's. Evidence: both test programs compiled cold under the default and under `-XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions -XX:hashCode=0`: the same 14 and 10 jar entries, every entry's bytes the same ('entries whose bytes differ between the modes: 0', REPORT.md section 4). What it means: row 996's order does not reach these names.
5. **On the rung's code the planner's measure of the one library refuses 12 declarations, 746 emitted, in 3 kinds; the kind 'a closure class written twice' is gone.** Conditions: `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-31/probes/planner/codegen-measure.sh` on a scratch worktree seeded at `39f833b8e5`; the before is F-34's run on `d3747846c1`, the base's code (13, 745, 4 kinds, `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-33/probes/measure-d3747846c1.txt:27-29`). Evidence: 'refused declarations 12 | emitted (OK lines) 746 | component failures 0'; ' 10  Can't compile VarArgs yet  [String 4, FortressLibrary 3, List 2, FlatString 1]'; '@@CG OK TraitDecl LexicographicOrder .../Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2301:1-2313:2'; '@@CG FAIL TraitDecl List .../Library/List.fss:106:1-174:2 ... NamingCzar.makeBoxedTupleName:1342 ... Can't compile VarArgs yet'. What it means: `LexicographicOrder`, which the compiled `=` on two integers names (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-31/probes/switch-rehearsal.md:110-118`), is emitted; `List`'s trait stops at a second wall, varargs (row 624, rung G).

# Rung G, climb batch 33b: record lines

## Findings

1. **The code generator compiles a varargs parameter against the one library as one immutable array of the arguments that no plain parameter takes.** Conditions: under `FORTRESS_LIBRARY=one`, or wherever the compile command's names point to `FortressLibrary`; a declaration at top level, in a trait or object, or local to a block, and an operator. The varargs part of a domain is one JVM parameter of `ImmutableArray[\T, ZZ32\]` of the library in use, after the plain parameters (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/NamingCzar.java:945-968`); the caller makes the array with the library's `__immutableFactory1[\T, 0, k\]()` and puts each further argument at its index with `init`, in order (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:7695-7831`). Evidence: `one_library_tests/OneLibraryVarargsCount.test`, `OneLibraryVarargsMethod.test`, `OneLibraryVarargsOperator.test`, `OneLibraryVarargsLocalFunction.test`, each failing on the base ('Can't compile VarArgs yet', `OptionUnwrapException`, 'Index 0 out of bounds for length 0') and passing on `4526151e00` (`OK (6 tests)` with the run test); the bytecode of `count(4, 5, 6)` in `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-varargs/REPORT.md`, "The convention as built". Meaning: row 624 closes under the selector; `println`'s path through `WriteStream` compiles.
2. **Where another declaration of the name takes as many arguments, the call goes to the dispatch method of that arity, whose branch for the varargs declaration makes the array.** Conditions: a top-level function or operator without static parameters; the dispatch methods hold the varargs declaration at each number of arguments from its plain count to the most another member takes (`CodeGen.java:8514-8541`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java:187-244`, `:2024-2033`); beyond, and for a generic declaration, the call makes the array. Evidence: `one_library_tests/OneLibraryVarargsOverloaded.test`: `check(z, z)` calls the dispatch method `check(Any;Any)`, `check(z, z, "a")` makes an array of one; the library's `assert(z, z)` calls `FortressLibrary.assert(Any;Any)`. Meaning: the expansion rule of `Specification/basic/overloading.tex`, "Applicability for Functionals with Varargs and Keyword Parameters", is how the compiled dispatch reads a varargs declaration.
3. **Against the compiler's prelude the code generator refuses a varargs declaration, naming the missing array type.** 'Can't compile VarArgs yet: the library in use, CompilerLibrary, declares no ImmutableArray, the type of a varargs parameter' (`NamingCzar.java:945-951`). Evidence: `compiler_tests/XXXVarargsCodeGeneration.test` (unchanged) and `XXXVarargsMethodCodeGeneration.test` (its message, from `OptionUnwrapException`), both expected failures on `4526151e00`. Meaning: P-37 holds; row 604's checker refusals stand beside it.
4. **On the code of `888c20dd93`, the planner's measure finds 3 refused declarations of the fourteen components, 751 emitted, in 2 kinds; the ten of varargs are emitted, `Generator2` and `CatString` among them.** Command: `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-31/probes/planner/codegen-measure.sh <scratch-worktree> <out-dir>`; output 'refused declarations 3 | emitted (OK lines) 751 | component failures 0', the closure class twice (row 315) and `__bigOperator2` (row 1076). Meaning: NEW-G-1; the specification's examples `f(1, [2 3]...)` do not run on either path.
6. **The code generator makes the one library's `ZZ32` from a JVM int as `FZZ32.make`, where the one library's descriptors name `fortress/FortressLibrary$ZZ32`.** Conditions: under the selection; the varargs array's indices (`CodeGen.java:7823-7825`), as `forIntLiteralExpr` (`CodeGen.java:4636-4642`) and the numeral sites (`FZZ.make` values passed to `coerce_ZZ32?natural`, whose descriptor names `fortress/FortressLibrary$ZZ`). Evidence: `javap -c -p` of `OneLibraryVarargsCount$task0` (`invokestatic FZZ32.make` before `init:(Lfortress/FortressLibrary$ZZ32;...)`). """The record's tool: it owns the form of FACTS.md and POSITIONS.md and of
their two history files, and is the only way to write them.

An entry is one line under a permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.` in
explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md and `- P-48 **Title.** Text.` in
POSITIONS.md. A number is never reused or changed: a new entry takes the
highest number its file has ever used, plus one. An entry stands under the
nearest `## ` or `### ` heading above it, its section. Its title is its bold
opening, or where it has none, its opening words up to the first colon,
semicolon or full stop.

A pointer is another entry's number in the sentence that needs it, alone
(`It builds P-48.`) or with the first words of the target's title in quotes
(`It builds P-48, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix ..."`, or
`P-48 ("...")`). Quoted words must open the target's current title (`...` or
`…` marks words left out); when an entry is retitled, the tool rewrites them
in every entry that points to it, in the same call.

The history (FACTS-history.md, POSITIONS-history.md beside the record) holds,
under `### F-87`, one block per change, oldest first: one provenance line (the
UTC time from the clock, the kind of change, `from` each report section,
`commit`, `by`, then the note after a colon), and the line as it stood before
the change. The tool derives the kind: `added`, `rewritten`, `moved to "S"`,
`merged into F-n`, `F-n merged in`, `removed`, `noted`; the numbering wrote one
`numbered` block per entry. A retitle that refreshed other entries' pointer
words, or a merge that moved their pointers, says so in one more line of the
block (`pointer words refreshed in: F-12, P-48`).

A `noted` block, which `note` writes, leaves the entry as it is. It adds what
the entry's history lacks, such as the curator's messages behind a text kept
word for word, with their times, or a correction of an earlier block. It holds
no earlier line, and its note says what it adds, so it needs one. A gone entry
takes none: its last block stays `merged into` or `removed`. A noted block
that corrects an earlier block names it by its time, in the field after the
kind: `correcting the block of 2026-10-13 19:07Z`, or, where blocks of the
entry share that minute, `correcting the 2nd block of 2026-10-14 04:41Z`,
counted oldest first. The block corrected is never edited.

content.content:
Every write takes a lock (flock on .record.lock beside the record), checks the
state it would leave, appends the history blocks first and then replaces each
record file in one step. A write is refused only for what would break the
store: a bad number, a pointer that does not resolve or whose words do not
open its target's title, a line break in an entry, no provenance (neither
`--from` nor `--note`; for a noted block, no `--note`), a correction that
names no block or more than one, two blocks for one entry in one call.
Never for size. The tool does not commit: commit the record file and its
history together.

usage: record.py COMMAND [ARGS] [PROVENANCE] [--root DIR]

  PROVENANCE: --from PATH#HEADING (repeatable; PATH from the repository root
  or from explorations/, HEADING held by exactly one heading of it, as doc:
  resolves one), --commit HASH (in HEAD's history), --by WHO, --note WHY.
  Each write needs --from or --note.

  add F|P --section TITLE FILE   a new entry from FILE's one line, numbered
      record.py add F --section 'Landed semantics' new.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The fix' --by coordinator
  set N [FILE] [--section TITLE] entry N rewritten from FILE's line, or moved
      record.py set F-87 f87.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The question' --note 'cut to the form'
  merge N --into M [FILE]        N removed, M rewritten from FILE (or kept),
                                 every pointer to N made a pointer to M
      record.py merge F-90 --into F-87 f87.md --note 'one fact, two entries'
  remove N                       N removed; refused while a pointer to it remains
      record.py remove P-131 --note 'evicted to the coordinator skill, references/briefing.md'
  note N [--correcting TIME]     a noted block in N's history, N unchanged; needs
                                 --note; refused when the history holds it already.
                                 TIME: 2026-10-13 19:07Z, or 2nd 2026-10-14 04:41Z
      record.py note P-25 --from 'positions-audit/full/evidence/corrections-c1.md#History lines the tool cannot write' --note 'his message behind the text: 2026-09-26T08:01:03.475Z, ...'
      record.py note P-7 --correcting '2026-10-13 19:07Z' --commit b87a17de5 --note 'that block names bc8902f47, ...'
  apply FILE                     many changes from one file, all or none (below)
      record.py apply chunk3.md --by 'consolidation chunk 3'
  check [--base COMMIT]          the store's checks; exit 1 on a failure
      record.py check --base cc9424c2a

An apply file holds, in any order: `## TITLE` or `### TITLE`, the section the
new entries below it go to (an existing entry stands under no heading, or
under its own section's, or the `## ` one that holds it); entry lines as they
should stand, `- F-87 ...`, or `- F-?1 ...` for a new entry, its placeholder
replaced by its number everywhere in the file; `move F-87 to SECTION`;
`remove F-90`; `merge F-91 into F-87`; `note F-87`, or `note F-87 correcting
TIME`, a noted block. Each may be followed by one indented provenance line of
its own:
`  from: PATH, "HEADING"; commit: HASH; by: WHO; note: WHY`. Blank lines and
`<!-- -->` comments are ignored. An entry line equal to the entry is skipped:
to add to its history, write `note F-87`. A note whose block the history holds
already, all but its time, is skipped too, so a file run twice writes nothing
twice. One call writes one block per entry, so an entry is noted, or changed,
once in a file.

check fails on: an entry line without its number, or a line under an entry
that continues it; a number on two lines; a number with no `numbered` or
`added` block, or one gone from its file whose last block is not `merged into`
or `removed`; a noted block that holds an earlier line, or whose `correcting`
names no earlier block of its entry, or more than one; a pointer to no live
entry, or quoted words that do not open the target's title; with --base, an
entry at COMMIT that is neither its line now nor the earlier line of a block
in its history (pointer words refreshed by the tool aside). It reports, without failing: the entries over 600 characters, the
entries without a bold title, and the `--from` paths and the report sections
an entry cites (`PATH`, "HEADING") that do not resolve.

The reads are facts-extract.sh's: `F-87`, `F-87+` (with the entries it points
to and that point to it), `history:F-87`, and the title queries, which fall
back to the former titles in the history.
"""

entries.name: TaskCreate
entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

subject.description: A brief title for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the task

entries.name: TaskUpdate
entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.

content.content:
# Rung N: the prelude's seven number types as value objects over payload classes

- problem: a program's object below the prelude's open trait `ZZ32` compiled and died when its class loaded, 'IncompatibleClassChangeError: ... can not implement ...FZZ32, because it is not an interface' (row 866), `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:1027`
- spec: "an object trait type cannot be extended. Thus, an object trait type excludes any type that is not its supertype", `Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:285-288`
- precedent: the one library's `value object ZZ32` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:846`), built as the planner's probe built form 2 in scratch, `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-33/probes/form2-prelude.patch:1`
- deviation: a payload object's RTTI keeps the object's class as its class and names its type by the payload class through a generated `className()`, where the probe made the payload class the RTTI's class, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:6283-6292`
- deviation: the names table follows the selector with no entries for the one library (fork N4), where the probe named `fortress.FortressLibrary$ZZ32` under the selector, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/LibraryNames.java:30-32`
- deviation: a payload class finds its object's class lazily, in holder classes, so that loading or initialising the payload class never fails, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FZZ32.java:51-62`
- deviation: the table of payload objects is keyed by the declaring api, a bare name read in the library that the compile reads, where the probe tested `WellKnownNames.fortressBuiltin()`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/NamingCzar.java:605-673`
- deviation: the cast to the object's class is the one cast of rung I's `castReceiver`, in both branches of `forMethodInvocation`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:7646-7654`
- deviation: the stub file's seven entries go, which the probe kept, `ProjectFortress/src/fortress/CompilerBuiltin.java:17-18`
- deviation: the run time's unit test of the array store boxes its own `ZZ32` payloads, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/ArrayStoreJUTest.java:65-66`
- historical: `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/NamingCzar.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/F{ZZ32,ZZ64,ZZ,NN32,NN64,RR32,RR64}.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/fortress/CompilerBuiltin.java`, `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXX6bx.test:13-19`

One launch of this role worked the rung. The worktree was seeded from `/home/user/fortress-base38` by `seed-worktree.sh` (exit 0, 4 s) and its branch pushed.

## What changed and why

P-178 makes each built-in number type one `value object` on both paths before the switch-over, the prelude by P-37's second exception; its detail, the carriers' review's way D, takes way C's machinery, and form 2 inside it: the code generator writes the object's class over a small hand-written payload class that extends nothing generated. The commits, on `wip/rung-number-payload-objects`: `d226bed17c` (tests first), `b9aa895753` (the change), `6465bd6678` (row 496's ZZ32 test promoted), `18f5a81d9b` (an expected failure measured on the way, row 1080), `c29eae9933` (a test of today's refusal of an excluded `typecase` clause, row 1081).

1. **The prelude's text.** `CompilerBuiltin.fsi:103`, `:147`, `:210`, `:273`, `:332`, `:401`, `:444` and `CompilerBuiltin.fss:516`, `:577`, `:662`, `:753`, `:818`, `:893`, `:955`: `trait ZZ32 extends { Number, Equality[\ZZ32\], StandardTotalOrder[\ZZ32\] } excludes { ZZ64, RR32, RR64 }` becomes `value object ZZ32 extends { Number, Equality[\ZZ32\], StandardTotalOrder[\ZZ32\] }`, and the same for `ZZ`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64`, `RR64` and `RR32`. Each `excludes` clause goes, since an object excludes every type that is not its supertype (`types-vals-vars.tex:288`). No body changed: `git diff c799851472 -- ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin` shows 14 lines, the seven headers in each file.
2. **The payload classes.** `runtimeValues/FZZ32.java` and its six siblings become `public abstract class FZZ32 extends FValue`, with the value field, a protected constructor, `getValue()`, `toString()` and the rest as before (`asString`, `makeSize`, `plus`, `make(BigInteger)` where the base had them). `make(x)` calls the object's class's static `make` through a method handle (fork N2), held in a nested `Make` class; the nested `RTTIc.ONLY`, which the run time reads for a static argument named by the payload class (`runtimeSystem/MethodInstantiater.java:137-141`), is the object's class's static `RTTI`. Both are found by the name that the new `runtimeValues/LibraryNames.java` gives (`:30-32`): `fortress.CompilerBuiltin$ZZ32` where the compiled path reads the prelude, and none where `WellKnownNames.compiledPathUsesOneLibrary` selects the one library (fork N4), where a value made raises 'The number type ZZ32 of the library that the compiled path reads is not compiled over ...FZZ32'. The stub file `src/fortress/CompilerBuiltin.java` loses its seven interfaces (70 lines); the build's dependency pass removed their old class files from `ProjectFortress/build/fortress/`.
3. **The table of payload objects.** `NamingCzar.java:605-673`: one row per object (the declaring api, the name, the payload class, the payload's JVM type `I`, `J`, `Ljava/lang/String;`, `F`, `D`), and four lookups: `payloadFor` (`:644`), the payload class and JVM type of an object being compiled; `payloadObjectClass` (`:664`), the object's class for a type; `payloadObjectClassOfPayload` (`:653`), the object's class for a payload class; a bare name is read in the library that the compile reads (`inSelectedLibrary`, `:625`). The table of carried types (`:588-601`) is unchanged, so every descriptor still names a number type by its payload class (fork N1).
4. **The code generator.** `CodeGen.java`:
   - `forObjectDeclPrePass` (`:4930-4937`, `:4946-4950`, `:5054-5076`, `:5124`, `:5242`, `:5283`): a payload object's class extends its payload class, is no singleton, has no init method of its own, and gets the constructor `(I)V` that passes the value up and the factory `static make(I)LFZZ32;`; the field `payloadObjectSuper` (`:235`, copied in the private constructor at `:386`) holds the payload class while the class is written.
   - `dumpMethodChaining` (`:1052`, `:1062`): a payload object takes every trait's bodies by forwarders, the first trait's too, since its superclass is no springboard.
   - `methodCall` (`:645-649`): a call on a payload object's type names the object's class, which holds its methods; the opcode stays `INVOKEVIRTUAL` (`:639-644`), since the type is now an object.
   - `forMethodInvocation` (`:7412`, `:7438`) and `castReceiver` (`:7646-7654`): the receiver on the stack is cast to the object's class where the receiver's type, after rung I's choice of the conjunct (`:7332-7336`), is a payload object's; else to I's owner, if any. One cast where the two meet, in the generic-method branch too, whose finder call names the receiver's class through `methodCall` (`:7702`).
   - `RttiClassAndInterface` (`:6283-6292`): a payload object's RTTI class keeps the object's class as its `javaRep`, as every object's does, and overrides `className()` to answer the payload class's name, `com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FZZ32`, which is what compiled descriptors and stamped instances name (fork N3).
5. **The dispatch test.** `OverloadSet.java:1095-1097`, `emitInstanceOfNG`: the RTTI that a dispatch test reads for a static argument is the object's class's static field, since the payload class has none.

`javap` of the generated class: `public final class fortress.CompilerBuiltin$ZZ32 extends com.sun.fortress.compiler.runtimeValues.FZZ32 implements fortress.CompilerBuiltin$Number, ...Equality⟦FZZ32⟧, ...StandardTotalOrder⟦FZZ32⟧, ...ValueObjectMark` (the probe's reading, PROBES section 2), with `make(int)`, the constructor `(int)` and the object's methods; the jar's classes after the library order (`unzip -l default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/fortress.CompilerBuiltin.jar`):

    19251  2026-11-18 02:26   fortress/CompilerBuiltin$ZZ32.class
      353  2026-11-18 02:26   fortress/CompilerBuiltin$ZZ32$RTTIi.class
     1599  2026-11-18 02:26   fortress/CompilerBuiltin$ZZ32$RTTIc.class

No `$DefaultTraitMethods` springboard is written for the seven, since they are objects.

## The design as built (a point to report)

- **The payload classes:** `FZZ32`, `FZZ64`, `FZZ`, `FNN32`, `FNN64`, `FRR32`, `FRR64` in `compiler/runtimeValues/`, each `abstract` over `FValue`, holding `int`, `long`, `BigInteger` (made from its digits), `int`, `long`, `float`, `double`.
- **The table of payload objects:** `NamingCzar.payloadObjects` (`NamingCzar.java:614-622`), seven rows of the prelude's api `CompilerBuiltin`.
- **What the code generator writes for such an object:** a final class `fortress/CompilerBuiltin$T` extending the payload class and implementing the traits of its `extends` clause and `ValueObjectMark`; a constructor `(payload)V`; `static make(payload)` answering the payload class's type; forwarders for every trait's bodies; its own methods as instance methods; `getRTTI()` and the static `RTTI` field; an RTTI class whose `javaRep` is the object's class and whose `className()` names the payload class.
- **How Java code makes a value:** `FZZ32.make(int)` (and its siblings), which the wrapper generator (`compiler/nativeInterface/FortressMethodAdapter.java:139-155`), the helpers and the class loader's sizes (`FZZ32.makeSize`) call, reaches `fortress.CompilerBuiltin$ZZ32.make` through the method handle that `LibraryNames.factory` finds, by name, with the payload class's loader, without initialising the class.
- **The one name of a payload object's type:** the payload class, `com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FZZ32`, in every descriptor, in every stamped instance (`Box⟦com|sun|fortress|compiler|runtimeValues|FZZ32⟧`) and in the RTTI's `className()`. Only the class that holds the methods and the static `RTTI` field is the object's.

## Each place that names a payload object's type (a point to report)

| place | file and member | name it gives |
|---|---|---|
| descriptors, casts, `instanceof`, a `typecase` arm | `NamingCzar.java:588-601`, the table of carried types, read by `jvmTypeDesc` | payload class `FZZ32` |
| a generic instance's name at the compile | `NamingCzar.instantiatedGenericDecoration`, `genericDecoration`, through `jvmTypeDesc` | payload class |
| a generic instance's name at the run, from an RTTI | `runtimeSystem/RTHelpers.java:35-41`, `:174-175`, `RTTI.className()` overridden in the object's RTTI class, `CodeGen.java:6283-6292` | payload class |

<!-- Climb batch 33b, rung W (rung-closure-name-once): each function expression of a component gets a class name of its own where two share a source span; row 315. -->

# Rung W: one class name for each function expression

- problem: row 315, 'java.util.zip.ZipException: duplicate entry: LexSame$\=fn@5\!23-66.class' under the selector (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-33/PROBES.md:113`), and the one library's two refused declarations of that kind, `LexicographicOrder` and `List` (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-33/probes/measure-d3747846c1.txt:27-29`)
- spec: none; the specification names no class of a function expression: `grep -rn -i 'class file\|classfile\|class name' Specification/basic Specification/basic-lib` prints nothing. The form that meets the defect is the conditional operator's sugar, `Specification/advanced/subscripting.tex:90-91` ("x OP: y is syntactic sugar for x OP (fn () => y)")
- precedent: the per-component table that every nested code generator shares, numbered in the order the code generator meets its entries, `numeralCoercionSites` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:286-290`, `:396`, `:410`, `:7858`), and the shared set `localFunctionNames` (`CodeGen.java:4237-4239`); the first name at a span is the team's own form (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/NamingCzar.java:901-907`)
- deviation: a later function expression at a span already named takes `#2`, `#3` after the span, a character that no class name of the code generator held before (`NamingCzar.java:905-906`); for a generic one the class file is `...#2⟦⟧` (`CodeGen.java:3937-3946`)
- historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/NamingCzar.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java` (both in the team's last commit `a874948ac`; there `gensymArrowClassName` is at `NamingCzar.java:838-840` and its one call at `CodeGen.java:3448`)

Commits on `wip/rung-closure-name-once`: `17f3e7b17b` (the fix and its tests), `39f833b8e5` (a third case of the compiled test, a generic trait's method), and the commit that adds this report and `record.md`. One launch worked the rung.

## 1. What changed, and why

The code generator named the class of a function expression (`CodeGen.forFnExpr`) and of a local function (`CodeGen.localFunctionClosure`) by its component and source span alone: `desc + "$fn@" + sp.toStringWithoutFiles()` (the team's `NamingCzar.gensymArrowClassName`). Two function expressions at one span got one name; the jar took the first class and the compile died at the second, 'ZipException: duplicate entry' (row 315).

Now `gensymArrowClassName(desc, sp, taken)` (`NamingCzar.java:893-907`) gives the first function expression of the component at a span today's name, and each later one at that span the name with the next ordinal, `#2`, `#3`, in the order in which the code generator meets them. `taken` is a set of the names given so far, one for the component: a field `closureClassNames` of `CodeGen` (`CodeGen.java:4241-4244`), made in the component's constructor (`:409`) and passed to every nested code generator (`:386`), as `numeralCoercionSites` and `localFunctionNames` are. The two calls pass it (`CodeGen.java:3935-3936`, `:4098-4099`). No other class's name changes, and no name of a program that compiled before changes: such a program had no two function expressions at one span.

## 4. The naming as built

- The thunk keeps today's name: `forFnExpr` names its class (`CodeGen.java:3935`) before it compiles the body (`:3970`), and the reduction's closure is inside that body, so the code generator meets the thunk first. The reduction's closure is `...#2`.
- The ordinal follows the order in which `forFnExpr` and `localFunctionClosure` are entered for the component. Two function expressions at one span lie in one declaration's body, one inside the other, so their order is the tree's; the order in which the code generator writes a class's methods or a dispatch method's tests (row 996) does not enter. The set is a `HashSet` that is only added to; its order is never read.
- The set is made with the component's `CodeGen` (`CodeGen.java:409`), so the names are the same from compile to compile, also in a JVM that compiled other components first, as the test suites' JVMs do.
- Shown: each test program compiled cold twice, once with `-XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions -XX:hashCode=0`, each in a fresh copy of the caches, the jars compared by `zipfile` (unzip rewrites the backslashes of the mangled names): the same 14 entries for `ConditionalReductionCompiled` and the same 10 for `OneLibraryConditionalReduction`, and every entry's bytes the same; both runs of the compiled program printed `PASS`.

      ConditionalReductionCompiled$\=fn@11\!64-89#2⟦⟧.class 51eff2df98 same bytes
      ConditionalReductionCompiled$\=fn@11\!64-89⟦⟧.class 4babf078d9 same bytes
      ConditionalReductionCompiled$\=fn@7\!36-50#2.class 867298951c same bytes
      ConditionalReductionCompiled$\=fn@7\!36-50.class f59505a2c9 same bytes
        entries whose bytes differ between the modes: 0 []

## 10. Sentences of the specification made false

None: no sentence of `Specification/` names a closure class, a duplicate class or a conditional operator over a reduction on the compiled path (`grep -rn -i 'duplicate entry\|closure class\|class name' Specification --include=*.tex` prints nothing; Appendix I's sentences on the code generator, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:255`, `:1732`, `:4046`, `:4440`, `:4607`, `:4689`, `:6396`, `:6409`, name other constructs).

## 16. Questions for the curator

None.

- F-? **A function expression's class, and a local function's, is named by its component and source span; a later one of the component at a span already named takes the name with `#2`, `#3`, in the order in which the code generator meets them.** The thunk that a conditional operator makes of its right operand takes the operand's span, and where the operand is a reduction, so does the reduction's outer closure `fn (reduction, unit) => ...`; the thunk is met first and keeps the span's name. So does the thunk that a binding `if` makes of its else part, where the else part is a reduction, and the function expression that an arrow coercion wraps around a function expression argument, met before the argument; three at one span take `#2` and `#3`. The set of names is one per compile of a component (`NamingCzar.gensymArrowClassName`, `CodeGen.closureClassNames`), so the names are the same from compile to compile and under another hash mode; a generic one's class file is `...#k⟦⟧`. On the one library this lets `LexicographicOrder` be emitted. Tests: `compiler_tests/ConditionalReductionCompiled.test`, `compiler_tests/ArrowCoercionFnExprCompiled.test`, `one_library_tests/OneLibraryConditionalReduction.test`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-closure-name-once/REPORT.md`, "4. The naming as built".

content.content:
# Rung G, climb batch 33b: a varargs parameter on the compiled path

- problem: the code generator refused every declaration with a varargs parameter and every call of one, ten of the thirteen declarations that the measure found refused in the one library, `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-33/probes/measure-d3747846c1.txt:16-25` (F-34; row 624)
- spec: `Specification/basic/functions.tex:210` ("Function Applications": the parameter holds the arguments that no plain binding takes, in order), `:183-200` (the revival callout: the type `ImmutableArray[\T, ZZ32\]`), `Specification/basic/overloading.tex:246` ("Applicability for Functionals with Varargs and Keyword Parameters": the expansion rule)
- precedent: walk's `NonPrimitive.buildEnvFromParams`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/values/NonPrimitive.java:224-251` (the factory `__immutableFactory1` at the count of the further arguments, `init` of each in order); the code generator's call of a generic function through its closure, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:4267-4289` and `generateHigherOrderCall`, `:7989`; the planner's stand-in for the JVM form, `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-33/probes/varargs-standin.patch:69-80`

- deviation: walk puts each argument through the array's wrapper (`IndexedArrayWrapper.put`); the compiled call names `init` on the parameter's type, `ImmutableArray[\T, ZZ32\]`, whose interface inherits it from `ReadableArray`, `CodeGen.java:7817-7828`

## What changed and why

The code generator refused varargs at four tuple descriptors of `NamingCzar` and in `forLetFn`, and stopped on a method's varargs parameter where `jvmSignatureFor` unwrapped its type (row 624). The value is fixed by the specification, its callout, F-86 and walk: an immutable one-dimensional array of the arguments that no plain parameter takes, typed `ImmutableArray[\T, ZZ32\]` of the library in use. The rung builds forks G1 to G5 of `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-33.md`, section 3.

1. **The declaration (G1).** The varargs part of a domain is one JVM parameter of `Types.makeVarargsParamType(T)`, the type at which the checker binds the parameter in the body (`NamingCzar.varargsParamType`, `NamingCzar.java:945-951`; `varargsDomainAsArray`, `:954-962`; `paramType`, `:965-968`). The four refusals now read the domain so (`:1344`, `:1354-1358`, `:1497`, `:1608`), as do the signatures over parameters (`:971-982`, `:993-1006`), the spliced signature of a trait's default method (`:1030-1031`) and the arrow descriptors from parameters (`:1259`). In the body the parameter is a local of the array type (`CodeGen.addParam`, `CodeGen.java:712`); two checks of a single tuple-typed parameter no longer unwrap a varargs parameter's absent declared type (`:3166-3167`, `:3296`). A local function's varargs refusal is gone (`forLetFn`, `:3998`), its arrow type takes the varargs part (`localFunctionArrowType`, `:4050-4051`), and its closure reads its parameters through the same `NamingCzar` members.
2. **The call (G2).** `evalArg` and `evaluateSubExprsAppropriately` (an operator's operands) send a domain with a varargs part to `evalVarargsArgs` (`CodeGen.java:7837-7840`, `:5725-5728`, `:7695-7750`). It evaluates the n arguments as the expansion rule reads the declaration at n, the plain types then the varargs type for each further argument, in parallel where the call's arguments fork. A single argument whose value is a tuple passes its elements, as the checker reads a tuple argument against a varargs domain (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:328-329`) and walk passes them (the skeptic's fix; `CodeGen.java:7701-7707`). Then, unless the call goes to a dispatch method, it stores the further arguments in compiler locals and `emitVarargsArray` (`:7795-7831`) makes the array: the factory `__immutableFactory1[\T, 0, k\]()` through its closure, then `init(j, a_j)` for j from 0, and the array is the call's last argument at the declaration's own signature.
3. **The dispatch method (G2).** `CodeGen.partitionByArgCount` (`CodeGen.java:8514-8541`) makes a varargs declaration without static parameters a member at each number of arguments from its plain count to the most that another declaration of the name takes, read there as an expanded declaration (`OverloadSet.VarargsExpansion`, `OverloadSet.java:187-244`). Its branch in the dispatch method loads the plain parameters, makes the array from the rest and calls the declaration (`armCallsVarargsDeclaration`, `:2024-2033`, from the arm path `:1869-1882` and the leaf `:1994-2013`). A call of n arguments whose name has a dispatch method at n passes the n arguments to it (`varargsCallDispatches`, `CodeGen.java:7759-7781`; the dispatch domain at the call, `forFunctionalRef`, `:4435-4443`).
4. **The prelude (G4).** `varargsParamType` refuses against the compiler's library, which declares no `ImmutableArray`: 'Can't compile VarArgs yet: the library in use, CompilerLibrary, declares no ImmutableArray, the type of a varargs parameter'.
5. **A spread argument (G3)** is not built; the parser takes it, and both paths drop it before the code generator (NEW-G-1). The code generator refuses one if it ever reaches it (`CodeGen.java:7696-7697`).

1. **The stages.** The section gives the rung none, and the brief says W and G run neither. `git diff --name-only c799851472...0b220e26e5` lists three paths outside the stage-blind folders, all of the code generator: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/NamingCzar.java`, `OverloadSet.java` and `codegen/CodeGen.java`. Both stages run the checker, which stops before the code-generation phase, and the edited `NamingCzar` members are the code generator's descriptors (`NamingCzar.java:936-1031`, `:1259`, `:1344-1358`, `:1497`, `:1608`); the checker's own uses of `NamingCzar` (the transfer helpers, `:373-384`, `:494-503`) are not touched. So no stage table exists, and none was owed. My fix edits `CodeGen.java` only.
8. **The ledger and the sibling sites.** Rows 11, 304, 314, 604, 623, 849, 978 and 1062 bear on the rung; 304 and 1062 are rewritten in `record.md`, 849 (a varargs `builtinPrimitive`) stands. The other reads of a parameter's declared type in the edited files are an object's constructor (`CodeGen.java:4979`, `:5092`, refused by the checker, row 11) and `OverloadSet.java:168-172`, `:912-925`, which an unexpanded varargs member reaches: row 1086.
The feature map's row for varargs (`explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:212`) names no code-generator site and the state 'code generation refuses varargs'; the checker passes these programs (F-86), so the fix is the code generator's alone: `NamingCzar` (descriptors), `CodeGen` (declarations and calls) and `OverloadSet` (dispatch methods), the files of the section. The gather may give the row its codegen cell (`NamingCzar.varargsParamType`, `CodeGen.evalVarargsArgs`, `OverloadSet.VarargsExpansion`). Walk's `buildEnvFromParams` is the precedent for the value. The ways the language and the library offer to carry the arguments: (a) one array parameter of the declared type, made by the caller; (b) one JVM method for each arity, writing the body again (fork G2's way not taken); (c) a JVM array of `Object`; (d) the array made by the callee from a `java.lang.Object[]`; (e) a library list (`<|...|>`). Only (a) gives the body the type at which the checker binds the parameter, so (a), as G1 says. For the array itself: the factory, as walk; `tabulate` would need a closure over the arguments; a native helper cannot make a library object. For the dispatch: the expansion rule's reading at each arity where another member meets it (G2), rather than one dispatch method with the packed signature that would branch on the array's length. The planner's stand-in (`probes/varargs-standin.patch`) rewrote every varargs parameter before code generation into a plain one; the rung reads the parameter's type at each place instead (`NamingCzar.paramType`), since the component index that the dispatch methods read keeps the declared parameters. Type 'fortress/CompilerAlgebra$\=StandardTotalOrder?...FZZ32?' (current frame, stack[1]) is not assignable to 'com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FZZ32''. The call resolves to `StandardTotalOrder[\ZZ32\]`'s generic `<`, its arguments are cast to that trait, and the static call now takes `ZZ32`'s own body, whose `self` is the class `FZZ32`; the base found no body there and dispatched. (* A call of a method that an imported api's trait declares twice, functional or dotted, whose every argument and receiver is a type assumption, runs the body that the assumed types choose (type-annotation.tex, section "Type Assumption"). *)
component AsIfApiTraitCompiled
import AsIfApiTraitApi.{ S, tag }
export Executable

object O extends S end
object P extends S
    tag(self, s: String): String = "p" || s
    m(s: String): String = "p" || s
end

run(): () = do
    k: ZZ32 = 1
    assert(tag(O asif S, "d" asif String), "sd", "tag(O asif S, d asif String)")
    assert(tag(O asif S, k asif ZZ32), "n", "tag(O asif S, k asif ZZ32)")
    assert((O asif S).m("d" asif String), "sd", "(O asif S).m(d asif String)")
    assert((O asif S).m(k asif ZZ32), "n", "(O asif S).m(k asif ZZ32)")
    assert(tag(P, "d"), "pd", "tag(P, d) runs P's own body")
    assert(tag(P asif S, "d" asif String), "sd", "tag(P asif S, d asif String)")
    assert(P.m("d"), "pd", "P.m(d) runs P's own body")
    assert((P asif S).m("d" asif String), "sd", "(P asif S).m(d asif String)")
    println("PASS")
end

end

run
